name: com.lapins.demo.invoicing.invoice
title: Invoice
description: Gives a Catalog product the meaning of an Invoice: a request for payment issued by a Merchant to a Payer, carrying a Doc Number, a Due Date and a Balance Due. The Merchant's invoicing system remains the sole system of record for every field here; this extension exposes those facts and stores none of them.

merchant.description: The business owed the Balance Due.

contact_email.description: Where a Payer takes a question about this Invoice.

payment_instructions.description: Free-text instructions the Merchant prints on its Invoices. Advisory: nothing in the protocol reads it.

payer.description: The party that owes the Balance Due. Identified by email because the reference product's Payer arrives on an unauthenticated link and holds no account.

invoice.description: Invoice facts as the Merchant's system of record reports them.

doc_number.description: The human-facing identifier printed on the Invoice. Opaque: not required to be numeric or sequential, and not usable as a sort key.

due_date.description: The day the Balance Due is payable by, as YYYY-MM-DD.

balance_due.description: The amount still owed. May be less than original_total when a partial payment has already been applied. This, not original_total, is what paying the Invoice settles.

original_total.description: What the Invoice was issued for, before any payment.

outstanding.description: Whether the Balance Due is greater than zero.

overdue.description: Whether an Outstanding Invoice's Due Date has passed. Overdue is a kind of Outstanding: a late Invoice is still owed, so both flags are true at once.

allowed_payment_methods.description: The instruments this Invoice will accept. Not uniform across a Merchant's Invoices.

dev.ucp.shopping.catalog.search.title: Catalog Search with Invoice
dev.ucp.shopping.catalog.search.description: Catalog Search response whose products are Invoices. The extension keys itself by its own reverse-domain name, as the loyalty extension keys its memberships, so a product carrying it cannot collide with another vendor's meaning.
